content.text: blood collection in anterior chamber of eye
(space b/n cornea & iris) - blood may cover most or all iris/pupil, blocking vision partially or completely - USU
Spontaneous or ← trauma - traumatic: ruptured iris root vessel bleed - spontaneous: assoc w sickle cell dz
Comp: ↑IOP · rebleed · corneal staining · optic atrophy · accommodative impairment
HX: often blunt or penetrating trauma
PE: ↓visual acuity · blood in anterior chamber - may layer posteriorly when supine → apparent only when upright
ddx globe rupture: ocular emergency ← trauma - ⊕Seidel sign on fluorescein ("waterfall" ← aqueous humor leak · may be absent if ⍉upright) · Δvision · irreg pupil
ddx hypopyon: layering of WBCs in anterior chamber → intraocular infect (endophthalmitis) - after intraocular procedures or trauma - rare comp of untx corneal abrasion/ulcer
Prevent rebleed & ↑IOP: HOB elevated 30-45° (lrg hyphemas, settles RBCs ⍉occluding trabecular meshwork) · gentle ambulation
▪︎topical or PO agents to ↓IOP · antifibrinolytics (tranexamic acid · aminocaproic acid ↓rebleed) · corticosteroids · cycloplegics - directed by ophthalmology
ADMIT: >50% hyphema · sickle cell dz (↑comp) · anticoagulants
Stable for d/c: urgent ophthalmology f/u (reassess IOP · bleed)
: idiopathic IC HTN · space-occupying lesion (cerebral tumor, abscess) · ↑CSF prod · cerebral edema · severe HTN (grade IV)
swollen optic disc w blurred margins
S/SXS: acute onset intermittent HA · blurred vision
Transient visual obscurations (seconds, w positional Δ) ← transient ischemia of optic n. head
Dilated tortuous retinal veins can occur - ⍉defining (optic disc swelling = defining)
ddx glaucoma: ↑intraocular P (norm in idiopathic IC HTN) · gradual periph vision loss - ⍉transient obscurations
MC cause of permanent legal blindness & vision loss in older adults (esp. >75)
Wet occurs more rapidly & = more severe
– sm · round · yellow-white spots on outer retina (represent local deposits of extracell material)
) may slow progression but do ⍉reverse chgs
Acidic vs alkaline - remove toxic agent/environment - identify agent · potency · inj type
Acid: coagulative necrosis - corneal ulceration w limited depth - significant pain but USU less severe · self-limited
Alkali: liquefactive necrosis → deeper damage (cornea · iris · lens) - penetrates faster & deeper - irreversible blindness w.in min if untx - glaucoma comp
Hydrofluoric acid (glass etching · cleaning solutions): local inj + systemic ↓Ca²⁺ & ↓Mg²⁺ → cardiac dysrhythmias
S/SXS: mod-severe pain · ↓vision · conjunctival redness · photophobia · inability to open eyelid
DX: check pH after irrigation (norm 7.0-7.4) → further exam for extent of burns
TX (initial): tetracaine or proparacaine drops + copious NS or H2O irrigation of both eyes (Morgan lens or manual) - ensure ⍉penetrating eye inj 1st
HF acid antidote: topical Ca gluconate gel - ⍉most immediate step
⍉immediate H2O irrigation (exothermic): dry lime · elemental metals (Na · K · Mg · lithium · cesium · titanium tetrachloride) · phenol
